stories.title: New discovery reveals what may be holding back room-temperature superconductors
summary: A major breakthrough in superconductivity research has revealed that one of the essential ingredients for electricity to flow without resistance can exist at room temperature.

Scientists discovered that electrons can form stable pairs at much higher temperatures than previously understood, suggesting that a different obstacle may be preventing room-temperature superconductivity.

stories.title: Stormont department failing to protect wild birds, investigation finds
summary: The Office for Environmental Protection said Daera had not complied with environmental law requiring it to classify and update Special Protection Areas.

stories.title: MIT discovers that aging weakens the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
summary: MIT researchers have discovered that the brain’s natural waste-removal system becomes significantly less effective during sleep as people age.
The decline is linked to weaker deep-sleep brain waves and changes in blood flow, potentially offering new clues about why aging increases the risk of Alzheimer's disease and dementia.
Surprisingly, some older adults retain the same powerful cleansing waves seen in younger people.

stories.title: A little-known protein could be a powerful weapon against Alzheimer’s
summary: Scientists have uncovered a powerful natural defense against Alzheimer’s disease that could open the door to new treatments.

By boosting a protein called SORLA, researchers significantly reduced toxic tau tangles, protected connections between brain cells, and prevented some of the brain shrinkage associated with neurodegeneration in mice.
Removing the protein made the damage worse, highlighting its critical protective role.

stories.title: William and Kate honour Earthshot Prize winners in Mumbai
summary: The Prince and Princess of Wales have said environmental innovators are changing the lives of future generations as they celebrated this year's winners of the Earthshot Prize.

stories.title: I want to know if toxic lagoon fire caused my husband's rare deadly cancer
summary: Steve Williams died of lung cancer 14 years after falling in to a lagoon at a toxic waste dump fire.

stories.title: People asked for views on blue brook pollution
summary: The Environment Agency wants to know how the incident affected visitors, residents and businesses.

stories.title: More than a billion years of Earth's history vanished. Scientists may finally know why
summary: Scientists may have finally explained why up to more than a billion years of Earth's geological history are missing from rocks around the world.

New research suggests that powerful currents deep inside the planet slowly raised and lowered entire continents, allowing erosion to erase vast stretches of geological history before they were buried and preserved.

stories.title: Conservationists searching for large river eels
summary: The Tees Rivers Trust has been searching for eels to tag and track as they migrate out to sea.

stories.title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?
summary: The BBC looks at why in a dry summer with few sewage spills, one bathing site failed so many water quality tests.

stories.title: Bizarre deep-sea fish with a see-through head captured in stunning 4K
summary: Deep-sea researchers have captured stunning new footage of an extraordinarily rare fish with a transparent head and rotating eyes nearly 2,000 feet beneath the ocean's surface.
Known as the barreleye fish, this bizarre creature uses its upward-pointing eyes to spot prey before rotating them forward to track its next meal, all while a transparent dome protects them.

stories.title: 125,000 years ago, hippos roamed what is now the vast Arabian Desert
summary: A remarkable 125,000-year-old discovery in Saudi Arabia reveals that early humans once thrived beside enormous lakes filled with wildlife in what is now a vast desert.
Thousands of stone tools and ancient plant remains suggest these prehistoric people used sophisticated hunting techniques, potentially including weapons enhanced with poisonous plant compounds.

stories.title: Autistic brains look surprisingly similar on average. Then scientists looked closer.
summary: Scientists discovered that although people with and without autism show surprisingly similar average brain activity, individuals with autism exhibit much greater differences from one another, especially in regions involved in social understanding.
The findings suggest that traditional research methods may be overlooking crucial differences that could help unlock more personalized autism support.

stories.title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns
summary: The UK could miss legally binding climate targets if EV targets are cut, an adviser warns

stories.title: Pakistan's solar revolution is so successful the national grid is lagging behind
summary: People installing their own solar panels has helped boost the solar share of Pakistan's electricity from 1% to 28%.

stories.title: Fears toxic lagoon fire led to cancer and miscarriages
summary: The incident took place in Llwyneinion in August 1980.

stories.title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court
summary: It follows years of debate over the alleged impacts on rivers in an area dubbed "poultry capital".

stories.title: A mysterious twist in the universe’s oldest light could reveal new physics
summary: Scientists have spotted hints of a mysterious rotation in the universe’s oldest light that could reveal new physics and shed light on dark matter and dark energy.
A new technique developed at UC San Diego could help rule out misleading telescope errors, bringing researchers closer to determining whether the strange signal is real.

stories.title: Giant lunar sculpture has visitors over the moon
summary: People can see the 6m-wide sculpture in St Helier until 29 November.

stories.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
summary: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful.
Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.

stories.title: The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected
summary: Scientists have discovered that psychopathic traits are associated with surprisingly different patterns of language, with some individuals using more positive words and others expressing greater negativity or less anxiety.
The findings challenge familiar stereotypes about psychopathy and suggest that the stories people tell about their lives may offer important clues about their personalities.

stories.title: ESA’s Hera spacecraft is flying rectangles around NASA’s asteroid crash site
summary: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has arrived at the scene of NASA’s historic asteroid collision to uncover what really happened when a spacecraft slammed into Dimorphos in 2022.
Its close-up investigation could reveal whether the impact left a crater or reshaped the asteroid entirely, providing crucial clues for protecting Earth from future threats.

stories.title: More than £160m needed to clean up one of Europe's largest illegal dumps
summary: Environment Minister Andrew Muir has described what happened at Mobuoy, near Derry, as an "absolute scandal" which could take a generation to fix.

stories.title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night
summary: The Leonid meteor shower, known for its bright and fast meteors, is set to peak on Tuesday night.

summary: Snow could bring some transport disruption to the hills of northern England and southern Scotland, as Chris Fawkes explains.
